instruction: Owner production policy uses three dynamic tiers with fixed counts only. Tier 1 / release-confirmed must contain exactly 2 games, Tier 2 / development-confirmed exactly 3 games, and every remaining game is Tier 3 / design-only. No game ID or title is permanently pinned to a tier. Company Status Sync reevaluates membership from current development-focus evidence, Artbook baseline maturity, real source availability, playable evidence, and real Unity-project readiness; stronger evidence may promote a game and the displaced game automatically demotes so the 2/3 counts never expand. Tier 1 production targets Unity Android. Exactly one of the two current Tier 1 games receives deep focused development at a time, selected automatically from current Tier 1 readiness and score; the other remains next-focus while its living Artbook/design is refined. Tier 1 preserved Web builds are archives and may receive FAST runtime-incident recovery only, not new Web feature development. Tier 2 produces a real Web first playable implementation/vertical slice and does not need to reproduce every Artbook feature in the first implementation. Tier 3 receives Artbook, concept, identity, story, system architecture, UI/UX and balance design optimization only; autonomous source-code development is forbidden, while existing public Web builds remain preserved as archive/evidence. Artbooks are living versioned design blueprints for all tiers and continue revision/baseline upgrades as implementation, QA, balance, story, technical or content evidence changes. ARTBOOK FIRST remains the production gate, but tier membership is evidence-ranked and is not locked to the current snapshot. Runtime incidents use the existing lightweight FAST lane for eligible Tier 1 or Tier 2 games: development and QA review, development owns the code change, and independent final QA/release gates remain mandatory. The latest play-impact priority signal remains active inside Tier 2 work selection so repeatedly low-impact floors lose queue priority rather than consuming repeated work. Vibe2 remains the company-wide production/analysis/verification engine. Five departments review normal floors independently in parallel; planning-final integrates and assigns file ownership; development, graphics, QA and balance may modify disjoint scopes in isolated workspaces; NO_SCOPE is normal. Source workers never write main directly. Verified candidates use the existing independent promotion/release gate and Public Health before release success; verified results feed Company DNA/Vibe learning and may trigger Artbook revision. The director enforces owner-immediate priority, verifies real execution evidence, resolves low-risk stopped-workflow bottlenecks without duplicate runs, and never ghostwrites missing specialist work or bypasses QA. Existing public Web builds and save meanings are not deleted by tier movement. Unity Android build success still requires a non-empty APK and SHA-256. Paid AI, paid overage and paid runners remain forbidden.
